subject: General Knowledge
description: More inventors + discoveries: antibiotics, transistor, internet, X-rays

questions.explanation: Wilhelm Röntgen — German physicist, discovered X-rays accidentally in 1895 while experimenting with cathode rays. First Nobel Prize in Physics, 1901. Named 'X' since nature was unknown. Quickly applied to medical imaging.
questions.subject: General Knowledge

questions.stem: The TRANSISTOR was invented in 1947 at Bell Labs by:
questions.explanation: Bardeen, Brattain, Shockley — Bell Labs, 23 December 1947. Nobel Physics 1956. Replaced vacuum tubes; foundation of modern electronics. Bardeen also won a 2nd Nobel (for BCS theory of superconductivity) — only person with two physics Nobels.
questions.subject: General Knowledge

questions.stem: The STEAM ENGINE — central to the Industrial Revolution — was refined by:
questions.explanation: James Watt — improved Thomas Newcomen's 1712 atmospheric steam engine by adding a separate condenser (1769) + sun-and-planet gear + double action. Made engines far more efficient. Unit 'Watt' (power) named after him. Spurred the first Industrial Revolution. who added separate condenser, late 18th c.

questions.stem: Match the INVENTION with its INVENTOR. A. Dynamo (electrical generator).  B. Incandescent bulb.  C. Radio (long-distance).  D. Powered airplane. List-II: 1. Michael Faraday.  2. Thomas Edison (with Swan).  3. Guglielmo Marconi (1890s).  4. Wright Brothers (1903).
questions.explanation: Faraday (1831) — electromagnetic induction, first dynamo. Edison + Joseph Swan (independently) — practical incandescent bulb (1879). Marconi — wireless telegraphy / radio (1890s-1900s). Wright Brothers — first sustained powered flight, 17 December 1903 at Kitty Hawk.
questions.subject: General Knowledge

questions.stem: The INTERNET evolved from which military research network?
questions.explanation: ARPANET — Advanced Research Projects Agency Network. Began 1969 with 4 nodes (UCLA, Stanford, UCSB, Utah). TCP/IP (Vint Cerf + Bob Kahn) protocols adopted 1983. NSFNET later supplemented and commercialised in the 1990s. Tim Berners-Lee invented WWW on top of this (1989-91 at CERN). US Defence, late 1960s.
questions.subject: General Knowledge

questions.stem: CRISPR — the revolutionary GENE-EDITING tool — earned the Nobel Chemistry 2020 for:
questions.explanation: Charpentier (French) + Doudna (American) — first all-female team to share a Nobel in the sciences. CRISPR-Cas9 = programmable gene-editing system. Huge potential + ethical concerns. Revolutionised biotech. Watson and Crick + Wilkins shared Physiology 1962 (DNA structure).
questions.subject: General Knowledge

questions.stem: The MRI (Magnetic Resonance Imaging) machine is based on the principle of:
questions.explanation: MRI — based on Nuclear Magnetic Resonance (NMR). Strong magnetic field + radio-frequency pulses align and perturb hydrogen nuclei (in water/fat) in tissues; signals emitted are mapped into images. Nobel Physiology 2003 (Lauterbur, Mansfield). No ionising radiation unlike X-rays / CT.
